findings.description: page is documented 1-based but offset = page * PAGE_SIZE, so the first page is skipped.
findings.scenario: list_orders(conn, cid, page=1) returns orders 21-40; the newest 20 orders are never returned on any page.

findings.description: Request-supplied status is interpolated into the SQL string with % formatting.
findings.scenario: status = "x' OR '1'='1" returns every order; status = "x' UNION SELECT ..." can read other data.
findings.fix: conn.execute("SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,))

findings.description: customer_id is passed in but never used; the order is looked up and cancelled by id alone, so any logged-in customer can cancel anyone's order.
findings.scenario: Customer A calls cancel_order(conn, order_id_of_B, A) and B's order becomes cancelled.
findings.fix: Scope both statements with AND customer_id = ? (SELECT and UPDATE), returning False if no row matches.

findings.description: Status is read in one statement and the UPDATE is unconditional on status, so the check can be stale.
findings.scenario: Order is marked shipped by another connection between the SELECT and the UPDATE; it is then overwritten to 'cancelled'.
findings.fix: Single statement: UPDATE orders SET status='cancelled' WHERE id=? AND customer_id=? AND status != 'shipped'; return cursor.rowcount > 0.

findings.description: ORDER BY a non-unique column with no tiebreaker makes LIMIT/OFFSET paging non-deterministic.
findings.scenario: Several orders share the same created_at or total_cents; rows can repeat or be skipped across pages.
findings.fix: Append ', id DESC' to the ORDER BY.
